label: Contract schemes
summary: A group of schemes (of the contract kind, going by its name) for the intrigue window to list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the intrigue window, so that block shows this group of schemes. The game documents nothing more.

label: Countermeasures
summary: The list of countermeasures the intrigue window offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the intrigue window, so the list shows one row per countermeasure. Going by its name, countermeasures are the options for defending against schemes. Its return type is not registered in the dump.

label: Current countermeasure
summary: The countermeasure currently in force, going by its name.
details: Vanilla's GUI and texts never use it, and its return type is not registered. The game documents nothing more.

label: Hooks on me
summary: The list of hooks other characters hold on the viewing character.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the intrigue window, and shows or hides parts of the window depending on whether the list has items or is empty. Going by its name, a hook is leverage someone else has over the character.

label: Hostile schemes
summary: A group of schemes (of the hostile kind, going by its name) for the intrigue window to list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the intrigue window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Known schemes
summary: The list of schemes the viewing character knows about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the intrigue window. Going by its name, these are schemes the character has found out about, as opposed to their own.

label: My hooks
summary: The list of hooks the viewing character holds on others.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the intrigue window. It also checks whether the list has items, and whether it has more than 4 entries, to decide what to show (together with an expand switch named hooks_expand). Going by its name, a hook is leverage over another character.

label: My secrets
summary: The list of the viewing character's own secrets.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the intrigue window and shows or hides parts of the window depending on whether it has items or is empty.

label: My strong hooks count
summary: The number of strong hooks the viewing character holds.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as text in the intrigue window. Going by its name, a strong hook is the stronger kind of hook, as opposed to a weak one.

label: My weak hooks count
summary: The number of weak hooks the viewing character holds.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as text in the intrigue window.

label: Personal schemes
summary: A group of schemes (of the personal kind, going by its name) for the intrigue window to list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the intrigue window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Political schemes
summary: A group of schemes (of the political kind, going by its name) for the intrigue window to list.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a block in the intrigue window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Puppets
summary: The list of puppets shown in the intrigue window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the intrigue window. Going by its name, puppets are characters the viewing character controls through schemes or hooks.

label: Secrets known to me
summary: The list of other characters' secrets the viewing character knows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the intrigue window, and shows a part of the window only while the list is empty. Going by its name, these are secrets the character has learned, not their own.

label: Strong hooks on me count
summary: The number of strong hooks others hold on the viewing character.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as text in the intrigue window.

label: Weak hooks on me count
summary: The number of weak hooks others hold on the viewing character.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as text in the intrigue window.

label: Has known schemes
summary: Whether the viewing character knows of any schemes.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show a grid of known schemes when true, and its negation to show a separate text part when false.

label: Has own schemes
summary: Whether the viewing character has schemes of their own, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has puppets
summary: Whether the intrigue window has any puppets to show.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to decide whether a part of the intrigue window is visible.

label: Is auto-assigning agents
summary: Whether the intrigue window's automatic agent assignment is switched on.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox, which ToggleAutoAssigningAgents flips. Going by its name, it concerns agents of schemes.

label: Is tab shown
summary: Whether the named tab of the intrigue window is the one showing.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla passes tab names such as 'schemes' and uses the result for the pressed look of the tab button and other parts of the window.

label: Cancel scheme
summary: Handler for a click that cancels a scheme in the intrigue window, going by its name.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action for click handlers. Vanilla passes the scheme of the clicked row. That it cancels that scheme is read from its name.

label: The intrigue window
summary: The intrigue window itself, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by how other Self functions are used in vanilla (passed as an argument, for example Character.Self), it gives the object itself. Vanilla's own lines do not use this one directly.

label: Switch tab
summary: Switches the intrigue window to the named tab.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla uses it with 'schemes' when the window opens and on tab clicks, including 'hooks_and_secrets'.

label: Toggle auto-assign agents
summary: Switches automatic agent assignment in the intrigue window on or off.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click of a checkbox whose checked state comes from IsAutoAssigningAgents.

label: This countermeasure
summary: The countermeasure row itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. Going by its name, it lets a GUI part reach this item as a whole. The game documents nothing more.

label: AI will-do value
summary: A number that, going by its name, shows how much the AI wants this countermeasure.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it in a label that starts with 'AI:' in the countermeasure list.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this countermeasure.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of a countermeasure row.

label: Countermeasure type
summary: The type of this countermeasure.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and asks it for its icon (GetType.GetIcon) to draw the texture of the row.

label: Is active
summary: Whether this countermeasure is the one currently in force.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of a selection halo icon on the row, and together with IsSelectable to decide whether the row ignores the mouse.

label: Is selectable
summary: Whether this countermeasure can be chosen.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable the row, often together with IsActive.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether this countermeasure is shown in the list.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the row.

label: This countermeasure item
summary: The countermeasure item itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used (passed as an argument), it gives the object itself.

label: Set countermeasure
summary: Chooses this countermeasure for a character.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click and passes the character shown by the intrigue window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the countermeasure is set for.

label: This hook item
summary: The hook row itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Hook character
summary: The character this hook row is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of parts of the hook row, so the pieces inside show that character.

label: Hook
summary: The hook this row shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the hook row.

label: This hook item
summary: The hook item itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used (passed as an argument), it gives the object itself.

label: This secret group
summary: The secret group itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can blackmail
summary: Whether the viewing character can blackmail with this group of secrets.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable a button and to choose between two texts in the blackmail tooltip.

label: Secret group character
summary: The character whose secrets this group holds.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context for parts of the secret group row. Going by its name and use, it is the character the secrets belong to.

label: First secret
summary: The first entry of this group of secrets.
details: Vanilla asks the result for its secret (GetFirstSecret.GetSecret) and uses that as a data context.

label: Secrets
summary: The list of secrets in this group.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list and checks that it has items before showing it.

label: Has unspent hooks
summary: Whether the group still has unspent hooks, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla shows the group when this is true or when the 'secrets_show_all' switch exists. What counts as an unspent hook is not documented.

label: This secret group
summary: The secret group itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used, it gives the object itself.

label: This secret item
summary: The secret row itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Known by
summary: The list of characters who know this secret.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the intrigue window, and a text counts its entries ("Known by N others").

label: Secret
summary: The secret this row shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the row, and its description is shown in the secret's text and tooltip.

label: Is expanded
summary: Whether this secret row is opened up to show more.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the extra parts. ToggleExpanded flips it, going by their names.

label: Is exposed
summary: Whether this secret has been exposed, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla's direct lines do not use it; similar lines use Scheme.IsExposed, which belongs to another type.

label: Is spent
summary: Whether this secret is spent, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla shows a secret when it is valid and not spent, or when the 'secrets_show_all' switch exists. What spent means is not documented.

label: Is strong hook
summary: Whether this secret is a strong hook for the given character, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla passes a character and uses the result as the visibility of a part of the row. What makes a hook strong is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the hook is checked for.

label: Is weak hook
summary: Whether this secret is a weak hook for the given character, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla passes a character and uses the result as the visibility of a part of the row. What makes a hook weak is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the hook is checked for.

label: This secret item
summary: The secret item itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used, it gives the object itself.

label: Toggle expanded
summary: Opens or closes this secret row, going by its name.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla does not use it for this type; same-named functions of other types are used on click to expand rows.

label: This inventory
summary: The inventory itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can equip
summary: Whether the given artifact can be equipped, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact, going by its name.

label: Can equip in slot
summary: Whether an artifact can be equipped in a slot, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it. It takes two arguments, presumably the artifact and the slot.

label: Can equip and replace
summary: Whether the given artifact can be equipped, replacing what is in its slot, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it in the royal court window, together with a check that the character is the local player, to enable a button for an artifact.

label: Artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts in this inventory.
details: Vanilla checks whether this list is empty to enable or show parts of the domicile and royal court windows. The faith window uses it on a holy site's inventory as the data model of a list.

label: Equipped artifacts text
summary: Text listing the artifacts equipped in a slot type, as used in a decision text.
details: Returns text. Vanilla calls it on a character's inventory after the words 'Currently Equipped:', with a slot type name such as 'primary_armament' and three more arguments, all 'NEWLINE'. What those three control is not documented (they look like separators).

label: Equipped slots text
summary: Text for the equipped slot count out of the maximum for the given artifact, going by its name.
details: Returns text. Vanilla puts it after the word Displayed (court artifact) or Equipped in the equipped-artifact line. The exact format is not documented; a count such as 1 of 2 is a guess from the name.

label: Artifacts in category
summary: The number of artifacts in one category of this inventory.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla uses it with 'inventory' and 'court' as the category.

label: Number of artifacts
summary: The number of artifacts in this inventory, going by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Artifacts for slot type
summary: The number of artifacts that fit a slot type, going by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Artifacts for slot type name
summary: The number of artifacts for a slot type given by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. The lines vanilla uses are on a path that goes through the character's inventory, and they show it as Owned in the commission-artifact decision, with names such as 'armor'.

label: Slot by name
summary: The inventory slot with the given name.
details: Vanilla uses it with names such as 'crown', 'journal' and 'regalia' as the data context of a slot in the inventory window.

label: Slot from type
summary: The inventory slot that belongs to the given slot type.
details: Vanilla passes the slot type selected in the royal court window and reads the artifact in the resulting slot.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a slot type, such as RoyalCourtWindow.GetSelectedSlot

label: Slots
summary: The list of slots of this inventory.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the slot list in the royal court window.

label: Has court artifact
summary: Whether the inventory holds any court artifact.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to choose between a normal tooltip for the court tab and a 'no court artifacts' text.

label: Has inventory artifact
summary: Whether the inventory holds any regular (non-court) artifact.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses its negation, together with other checks, as the visibility of a part of the inventory window.

label: Has artifacts of slot type
summary: Whether the inventory holds any artifact for the given slot type.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to dim empty slots and to choose tooltip texts.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a slot type, such as InventorySlot.GetType

label: Has equipped in slot type
summary: Whether an artifact is currently equipped in the slot type with the given name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses the same name, through the character's inventory, in decision texts with names such as 'pedestal' and 'wall_big'.

label: Has unequipped in slot type
summary: Whether the inventory holds artifacts of the given slot type that are not equipped.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of parts of the royal court window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a slot type, such as InventorySlot.GetType

label: Is empty
summary: Whether the inventory is empty, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla does not use it directly for this type; the lines found use IsEmpty on a slot, which is another type.

label: Is equipped
summary: Whether the given artifact is equipped.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it in the inventory and royal court windows for the pressed look and visibility of artifact rows.

label: This inventory
summary: The inventory itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used, it gives the object itself.

label: This slot
summary: The slot itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can hold artifact
summary: Whether this slot can hold the given artifact.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show only artifacts that fit the slot selected in the inventory window.

label: Slot artifact
summary: The artifact in this slot.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the holy site windows and checks that it is valid, to know whether the slot is filled.

label: Slot description
summary: The description text of this slot, going by its name.
details: Returns text. Vanilla does not use it directly for this type; the same name on other types gives their descriptions.

label: Slot name
summary: The display name of this slot.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a heading in the slot tooltips of the royal court, domicile and holy site windows.

label: Slot type name
summary: The name of this slot's type, as text.
details: Returns text. Vanilla passes it to a function that counts new artifacts for that slot type, to show a counter in the inventory window.

label: Slot type
summary: The type of this slot.
details: Vanilla uses it to draw the type's icon (GetType.GetIcon) and to pass the type to the inventory functions that check for artifacts of a slot type.

label: Has artifact equipped
summary: Whether the given artifact is equipped in this slot, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact, going by its name.

label: Is empty
summary: Whether this slot holds no artifact.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show filled or empty slots in the holy site windows.

label: This slot
summary: The slot itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it into functions that ask whether this slot is the selected one, for example in the domicile and holy site tooltips.

label: This slot type
summary: The slot type itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Slot type icon
summary: The icon of this slot type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an element in the inventory window.

label: Slot type name
summary: The display name of this slot type.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it in the tooltip of the artifact sorting tabs, followed by the word artifacts.

label: Slot type key
summary: The name of this slot type, as text.
details: Returns text. Vanilla passes it to a function that counts new artifacts for that slot type, to show a counter on the tab.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether this slot type has an icon, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type; similar lines of other types use HasIcon for visibility. Its return type is not registered.

label: Is inventory type
summary: Whether this slot type belongs to the regular inventory (not the court).
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of tabs in the inventory window. That it excludes court slots is inferred from its name.

label: This slot type
summary: The slot type itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the inventory view when a slot type tab is clicked or checked.

label: This inventory view
summary: The inventory window itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can equip in selected slot
summary: Whether the given artifact can be equipped in the selected slot, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact, going by its name.

label: Clear selected slot
summary: Deselects the slot chosen in the inventory window.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click handlers in the inventory window.

label: Close
summary: Closes the inventory window.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click of close buttons.

label: Equip
summary: Equips the given artifact, going by its name.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact, going by its name.

label: Artifact claims list
summary: The list of artifact claims shown in the inventory window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context for the claims part of the window. Going by its name, it covers claims on artifacts.

label: Artifact click tooltip
summary: The text that tells what clicking the given artifact does.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as a text line for an artifact row.

label: Sort options
summary: The list of ways artifacts can be sorted.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the sort dropdown in the inventory window.

label: Selected sort option
summary: Which entry of the sort options is selected.
details: Returns a pair of whole numbers (a two-part index). Vanilla uses it as the selected index of the sort dropdown.

label: Inventory owner
summary: The character whose inventory the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, and also asks it for the inventory (GetCharacter.GetInventory).

label: Number of artifacts
summary: The number of artifacts, going by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Number of court artifacts
summary: The number of court artifacts, going by its name.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Selected slot
summary: The slot currently selected in the inventory window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, and asks it for its type (GetSelectedSlot.GetType).

label: Sorted artifacts
summary: The list of artifacts in the order chosen by the sort options.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the artifact list and checks whether it is empty to show a message.

label: Slot types
summary: The list of distinct slot types, one each.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the slot type tabs in the inventory window.

label: Has selected slot
summary: Whether a slot is selected in the inventory window.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it, often negated, to enable or show parts of the window.

label: Is equipped in selected slot
summary: Whether the given artifact is equipped in the selected slot, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The artifact, going by its name.

label: Is sort descending
summary: Whether the artifact sort order is descending.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla turns it into a frame number (1 or 2) for the arrow icon of the sort button.

label: Is selected slot
summary: Whether the given slot is the selected one.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it for the pressed look and visibility of slots, and in the slot tooltip.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the inventory window is shown.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the window's visibility, together with a check that the barbershop is not open.

label: Click artifact
summary: Handles a click on the given artifact in the inventory window.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. What the click does is not documented.

label: Click slot
summary: Handles a click on the given slot in the inventory window.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. What the click does is not documented.

label: Click slot type tab
summary: Handles a click on the tab of the given slot type.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. What the click does is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The slot type of the clicked tab.
fields.values: a slot type, such as InventorySlotType.Self

label: Selected slot has type
summary: Whether the selected slot is of the given slot type.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it for the pressed look of the slot type tabs.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a slot type, such as InventorySlotType.Self

label: This inventory view
summary: The inventory window itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used, it gives the object itself.

label: Sort artifacts
summary: Sorts the artifacts in the inventory window by the chosen option.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it when the selection in the sort dropdown changes.

label: Toggle sort order
summary: Flips the artifact sort order between ascending and descending.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click of the sort order button.

label: Toggle selected slot
summary: Selects the given slot, or deselects it if it already is selected.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click of a slot. The deselect part is inferred from its name.

label: Unequip
summary: Unequips the given artifact.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click and passes the artifact in the slot.

label: This offer
summary: The claimant faction invitation offer itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: This offer
summary: The claimant faction invitation offer itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used, it gives the object itself.

label: This setting
summary: The GUI setting itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Setting description
summary: The description text of this setting.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as text in the settings window.

label: Setting changed
summary: Whether this game setting has been changed and not yet applied.
details: Vanilla shows the 'Requires restart' mark next to a setting's name when it is shown, this is yes, the settings window applies changes on restart and the setting needs a restart. 'Not yet applied' comes from that use and the name.

label: This setting
summary: The GUI setting itself, to hand to another function.
details: Vanilla's lines do not use this one directly. Going by how other Self functions are used, it gives the object itself.

label: Should show
summary: Whether this setting should be shown in the settings window.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of a setting, once alone and once together with the check that the setting needs a restart.

label: Game rule by name
summary: The game rule with the given name, as an object the GUI can read.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context with names such as 'difficulty' and 'gender_equality'. Its return type is a GUI game rule.

label: This game rules object
summary: The game rules object itself, going by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it for this type. The game documents nothing more.

label: Apply settings
summary: Applies the chosen game rule settings.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click of buttons in the game rules window.

label: Delete preset by index
summary: Deletes the preset at the given position in the preset list.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla passes the index of the selected preset.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a whole number, such as JominiGameRules.GetSelectedPresetIndex

label: Delete preset by name
summary: Deletes the preset with the given name.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla passes the name typed into the preset name field.

label: Categories
summary: The list of game rule categories.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the category list in the game rules window.

label: Invalid preset name tooltip
summary: The text that explains why the typed preset name cannot be used.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the save button when the name is not valid, and a normal tooltip otherwise.

label: Preset save name
summary: The preset name entered for saving.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in a text field and in the delete and overwrite tooltips.

label: Rule presets
summary: The list of saved game rule presets.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the preset list, and shows a part of the window when the list is empty.

label: Selected category
summary: Which game rule category is selected in the dropdown.
details: Returns a pair of whole numbers (a two-part index). Vanilla uses it as the selected index of the category dropdown.

label: Selected preset
summary: The game rule preset currently selected.
details: Vanilla reads its name for the dropdown text and asks it whether Ironman is enabled (GetSelectedPreset.IsIronmanEnabled).

label: Selected preset index
summary: The position of the selected preset in the preset list.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla passes it to the delete-by-index action.

label: Settings
summary: The list of game rule settings, going by its name.
details: Vanilla never uses it; the visible-settings sibling is used instead. Its return type is not registered.

label: Visible settings
summary: The list of game rule settings that should be shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the rules list in the game rules window. That it depends on the chosen category is not stated.

label: Has preset with name
summary: Whether a preset with the given name already exists.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla passes the typed name and uses the result to enable the overwrite button and to switch between save and overwrite.

label: Has rule with flag
summary: Whether a rule with the given flag exists, going by its name.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla does not use it for this type; the lines found call it on a game rule preset, with a flag named 'blocks_achievements'.

label: Has selected category
summary: Whether a category is selected in the dropdown.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show the category name or a 'none selected' text.

label: Has valid preset selected
summary: Whether a valid preset is selected.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show the preset name or a 'none selected' text, and to enable a control.

label: Hide
summary: Closes the game rules window.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on click of buttons in the game rules window.

label: Hide preset window
summary: Closes the preset window.
details: Returns nothing; it is an action. Vanilla runs it on a click in the game rules GUI.
